sprintName: Master Gradebook, Multi-Dimensional Analytics & Export Engine
goals: Deliver student personal quiz performance overview sorted by surname or score
Build Faculty Master Gradebook with mandatory separation of records by year level and section
Support PDF and Excel export generation with dedicated multi-sheet layouts

issues.title: [Gradebook] Student Personal Quiz Results Summary
issues.description: Student dashboard displaying personal quiz scores, passing status, breakdown of attempts, filterable and sortable by surname or score.
issues.implementationDetails:
### Implementation Architecture & Details

#### 1. Scope & Objective
Personal student performance dashboard displaying all completed quizzes, scores, attempts, and pass/fail statuses.

#### 2. Features
- Sortable by date, surname, and score (Requirement 7 & 7a).
- Visual 75% benchmark indicator (Passed in green, Needs Review in amber).
- Export personal results to individual PDF or spreadsheet report.

#### Verified implementation
- Personal results, retake numbering, date/surname/score sorting, pass indicators, summary distributions, and personal exports.

issues.title: [Gradebook] Faculty Master Gradebook with Mandatory Separated Records by Year Level & Section
issues.description: Faculty analytics matrix showing all student scores categorized into distinct, mandatory separated datasets/tabs for each Year Level and Section, with multi-column sorting (Surname, Score).
issues.implementationDetails:
### Implementation Architecture & Details

#### 1. Scope & Objective
Faculty Master Gradebook with mandatory separation of student records by Year Level and Section (Requirement 8).

#### 2. Data Segregation Architecture
- Dedicated separate datasets and tabs for each unique combination (e.g. "3rd Year · Section A", "3rd Year · Section B").
- Filterable by year level, section, student surname, and score ranges.

#### Verified implementation
- Faculty-owned subject scope; mandatory cohort-separated datasets and tables; aggregate performance metrics.

issues.title: [Export] PDF and Excel Spreadsheet Export Engine
issues.description: Generate clean, downloadable PDF reports and formatted Excel (.xlsx) spreadsheets for both student summary reports and faculty master gradebook tables.
issues.implementationDetails:
### Implementation Architecture & Details

#### 1. Scope & Objective
Automated document export pipeline for formatted PDF documents and Excel (.xlsx) spreadsheets for students and professors.

#### 2. Implementation Stack
- **Excel Export**: server-side `exceljs` generating styled tabular worksheets.
- **PDF Export**: `jspdf` + `jspdf-autotable` with academic institutional styling.

#### Verified implementation
- Authenticated server-side PDF and styled Excel export endpoints share the same scoped filters as the gradebook. ExcelJS supplies worksheet styling.

issues.title: [Gradebook] Faculty Multi-Dimensional Filter Engine with Mandatory Segregated Tabs by Year Level & Section
issues.description: Build high-performance table view segregating student records strictly by Year Level and Section into distinct tabs, with real-time multi-criteria filtering by surname search, score brackets, and completion status.
issues.implementationDetails:
### Implementation Architecture & Details

#### 1. Scope & Objective
Interactive multi-dimensional gradebook filtering engine strictly maintaining separate records per Year Level & Section.

#### 2. Capabilities
- Filter chips: Year Level (`1st Year` to `4th Year`), Section (`Section A` to `Section D`).
- Multi-column sort: Alphabetical by student surname, numerical by score percentage.
- Real-time search query matching student name, ID, or quiz title.

#### Verified implementation
- Year, section, subject, name/ID/quiz search, score-range and status filters; stable secondary sorting; separate cohort tabs; 25 attempts per cohort per page.

issues.title: [Export] Institutional Multi-Sheet Excel (.xlsx) Report Generator with Separate Sheets per Year Level & Section
issues.description: Implement automated workbook generation creating separate spreadsheet tabs/sheets for each Year Level and Section with formatted grade summary headers, average scores, and pass/fail indicators.
issues.implementationDetails:
### Implementation Architecture & Details

#### 1. Scope & Objective
Multi-sheet Excel workbook export generating distinct spreadsheet tabs for each Year Level and Section combination.

#### 2. Workbook Structure
- **Sheet 1**: "3rd Year - Section A"
- **Sheet 2**: "3rd Year - Section B"
- **Summary Sheet**: Overall cohort metrics, pass rates (>= 75%), score distributions, and averages.

#### Verified implementation
- Summary sheet, separate formatted cohort sheets, numeric percentages/dates, frozen headings, filters, pass/fail styling, cohort metrics and score distribution. Exports include all matching pages.

issues.title: [Export] Formal PDF Gradebook & Student Report Card Exporter with Institutional Branding & Verification Signatures
issues.description: Implement publication-grade PDF generation with institutional Quikz academic header, student alphabetical indexing by surname, score breakdowns, 75% benchmark badges, and certified faculty sign-off sections.
issues.implementationDetails:
### Implementation Architecture & Details

#### 1. Scope & Objective
Formal PDF report card and faculty master gradebook exporter formatted with academic styling and instructor signature lines.

#### 2. Layout Specifications
- Institutional Quikz header banner with course code, term, and date.
- Alphabetical student table sorted by surname with individual quiz scores and pass/fail badges.
- Formal academic certification block with faculty signature underline.

#### Verified implementation
- Institutional branding, cohort pages, course/term and score breakdowns, surname indexing, repeated headings, pagination and faculty verification signature lines. Three- and nine-page PDFs rendered and visually reviewed.

scopeUpdate.details: Original issue titles and acceptance text are retained as historical GitHub records. Fixed 10–20 minute total timing and 75% passing rules are superseded: new quizzes use faculty-set time per question in seconds/minutes, passing percentages from 1–100%, and 1–100 questions per attempt up to bank size. Runtime, progression, and reports use these settings; historical quizzes/results retain their prior timing and grading.
